la:other:Drusus.html:
Drūsus, i, m.,
a well-known Roman surname in the Livian family, first assumed by the Livius who slew the Gallic general Drausus, .—Esp.
M. Livius Drusus, uncle of Cato Uticensis, murdered by Q. Varius, ; .—
Claudius Drusus Nero, son of Tib. Claudius Nero and Livia Drusilla, father of Germanicus, the theme of ; ; .— Hence, Drūsĭānus, a, um, adj.: fossa,, or Drūsīnus, a, um, adj.: fossae,a canal on the Lower Rhine, constructed by Drusus, the son of Livia,.—Drūsilla, ae, f., the name of

several females of the Livian family.— Esp.

Livia Drusilla, the second wife of Augustus, v. Livius.—
Drusilla, daughter of Drusus Germanicus, ; ;

la:noun:drachma.html:
drachma (old form, drachŭma, like Alcumena, Aesculapius, ; ), ae (
gen plur. drachmūm, Müll.; usually drachmarum,; Cic. Fl. 19, 43), f., = δραχμή.
A small Greek coin, a drachma or drachm, of about the same value as the Roman denarius, Enn. ap. ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—
As a weight, the eighth part of an uncia, the half of a sicilicus, about the same as our drachm, ; Rhem. Fann. de Pond. 17 sq.
